payload.purpose: Deep codebase audit by a tightly coupled swarm (swarm a) for comparison with the root's audit

request.objective:
You are the lead of swarm audit-a in Baton, the cross-agent coordination harness this repository is. Your task: a deep audit of Baton's own codebase, run as a tightly coupled swarm, producing docs/audits/2026-09-14-codebase-audit/swarm-a/lead.md plus one report per worker in the same directory. The root orchestrator is running the same audit itself and with another swarm; the value of yours is what you find that they do not, and what you all find (the comparison is the root's job; be honest and specific, quote code with file:line).

Recruit three workers (you hold recruit), each with a short, concrete objective you write, all with options {"exact":{"harness":"omp","model":"deepseek/deepseek-flash","effort":"max"}} and permissions ["read","communicate","contribute"], sharing ONE checkout (shareWorkspaceWith the first):
- giants: impl/src/coordinator.mjs, coordination-store.mjs, coordination-internals.mjs, coordination-replay.mjs, contribution-service.mjs, contribution-verification.mjs, referee.mjs, worktree.mjs, worktree-capacity.mjs, log.mjs, process-lifecycle.mjs → giants.md
- surfaces: impl/src/application*.mjs, control-surface-unification.mjs, mcp-northbound.mjs, mcp-web-bridge.mjs, web-northbound.mjs, resident-authority.mjs, impl/scripts/baton.mjs, mcp-stdio.mjs, mcp-web.mjs, surface-gate.mjs, CLI.md, MCP.md, plus the harness adapters adapter.mjs, cli-adapters.mjs, omp-rpc.mjs, claude-session.mjs, codex-appserver.mjs, grok-acp.mjs, kimi-acp.mjs → surfaces.md
- swarm: impl/src/swarm-*.mjs, native-subagent-*.mjs, messages.mjs, docs/39-swarm-runtime.md, docs/36-unified-control-grammar.md, docs/audits/2026-09-13-runtime-policy/*.md, docs/audits/2026-09-14-swarm-communication/*.md, impl/scripts/run-suite.mjs, suite-verdict.mjs, expected-red-tests.json → swarm.md

Each worker reports, with file:line evidence and at most ~40 items: FRICTIONS (what an agent or operator must know or do that the code could do for them), GAPS (missing capabilities or unhandled cases), ERRORS (suspected bugs with a confidence level: races, silent failures, dead code, comment-vs-code contradictions, control decisions taken from prose or id shapes, duplicated derivations that drift, unbounded resource use), IMPROVEMENTS (narrow, well-engineered; never a hardcoded numeric limit as a control mechanism), NOVEL INSIGHTS (what no single file shows), and the 5 items it would fix first. Priorities: silent failures, non-converging waits, anything that makes the harness lie about its state, and the agentic experience of a participant inside a swarm and of an orchestrator using MCP or the CLI.

Declare the coupling honestly and use it: three units of work (giants, surfaces, swarm) plus a fourth "synthesis" with dependsOn all three; a synchronization point "reports-in" every worker arrives at when its report is written; an exclusive writer over the shared checkout while a worker writes its file (release it when done); a failure policy that lets the others continue if one worker dies and tells the synthesis. Coordinate only through the swarm (assignments, guides, watch, reviews); review each report (accept or comment with what is missing) before you write lead.md: your synthesis across the three (the ten findings that matter most, each with evidence and a proposed narrow fix), what the coupling records did for you and what they did not, refusals verbatim, timings. Publish swarm.contribution_recorded naming lead.md and end your turn so the root captures. Constraints: write only under docs/audits/2026-09-14-codebase-audit/swarm-a/; no source changes; do not run the full suite; a budget threshold notification is evidence, not a stop; never print environment variables containing tokens.

payload.body:
swarm.md written (docs/audits/2026-09-14-codebase-audit/swarm-a/swarm.md, 35 items, every claim file:line-quoted).

Headlines:
1. [reproduced] content.message wakes swarm watchers. The no-wake filter (swarm-runtime.mjs:474-478) excludes content.tool_call, route.observed and resource.* but NOT content.message — a kind the repo itself classifies as non-progress telemetry (application.mjs:88 NOISE_TELEMETRY_OPERATIONAL_KINDS). evidence.mapped payloads carry worker (coordination-store.mjs:12194) and the filter matches on payload.worker (swarm-runtime.mjs:482), so every OMP UI frame (omp-rpc.mjs:542-548: setStatus/setWidget/setTitle) wakes every watcher. Contradicts docs/39:160 and integration.md:26; the outside saw it (root.md:174) but nobody had the predicate. Verified by driving the real _watch with the real payload shape: content.message WAKES; content.tool_call and resource.tokens stay silent.
2. [reproduced] swarm.holder_released cannot land when the group it prunes still names another departed member. The planned group event (swarm-runtime.mjs:558) removes only the holder, then the trial fold (564-565) hits the fold's active-member check (swarm-state.mjs:435-439) and the whole batch records NOTHING — as an untyped SwarmIntegrityError — while the runtime's own attention rows name this operation as the next step (swarm-runtime.mjs:302,312) and docs/39:203 calls it one durable batch. Reachable via join -> group -> leave -> release. Filtering the roster to active members folds cleanly (verified).
3. [reproduced] An over-cap request sent without content-length (chunked) is answered with ECONNRESET instead of the typed 413: readBody calls req.destroy() (swarm-native-bridge.mjs:100) and sendJson then no-ops on the destroyed response (109). The same body with a truthful content-length returns the composed 413. native-swarm-access.md:180 claims the streamed case is covered; no chunked test exists.

Also: --write-expected-red rewrites the whole 449-row manifest from a partial run (run-suite.mjs:399-403, no explicitFiles guard); the verdict's lane-stall branch is unreachable (stalled hardcoded null at run-suite.mjs:398) yet pinned by suite-verdict.test.mjs:64-70; projectOmpParallelTasks, the three board factories and that branch are three tested pure functions with no production consumer.

Notes: I did NOT run the test suite (the audit contract forbids executing it), so 'test pins X' statements are reads; the three reproduced findings were executed against the real modules via node --input-type=module -e and the eval kernel, writing no file. The lead's protocol names a writer record over the shared checkout, but the swarm carries none (only sync-reports-in and policy-auditors) — I recorded context/writing:swarm, wrote on the documented rule that coupling informs and does not fence, and said so in the report. Nothing outside swarm.md was written.

Notes: no project suite run - the wave contract is a reading audit and the deliverable is docs-only, so the deployment verification command was deliberately not executed; probes ran outside the repo in /tmp only.
